query: Activation and expansion of human T cells using artificial antigen-presenting cell scaffolds
title: Activation and expansion of human T cells using artificial antigen-presenting cell scaffolds
markdown:
## Protocol: Activation and expansion of human T cells using artificial antigen-presenting cell scaffolds

### Overview

This protocol details the fabrication of artificial antigen-presenting cell scaffolds (APC-ms) using high-aspect-ratio mesoporous silica rods (MSRs) and liposomes, followed by the isolation, activation, and expansion of human T cells. The process involves synthesizing MSRs, preparing lipid bilayers, conjugating IL-2 and biotinylated ligands to the scaffolds, and utilizing these APC-ms to activate primary human T cells (either from PBMCs or purified Pan T cells). The expanded T cells can be maintained for analytical and functional assays.

### Materials/Reagents

- RPMI-1640 medium
- Heat-inactivated Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS)
- Penicillin/streptomycin
- Sodium pyruvate (100X)
- Non-essential amino acids (100X)
- HEPES (cell culture grade)
- β-mercaptoethanol
- Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO)
- Phosphate-buffered saline (1X PBS)
- Bovine serum albumin (BSA)
- EDTA (0.5M stock)
- Recombinant human IL-2 (BioLegend, typically 0.2 mg/mL)
- Streptavidin (VWR)
- Milli-Q water
- Mesoporous silica rods (MSRs)
- Tetraethyl orthosilicate
- Hydrochloric acid (HCl, concentrated)
- Pluronic P123 surfactant
- Ethanol (200-proof)
- Chloroform
- Isopropyl alcohol
- Lipids for liposome formation (including Biotinyl Cap PE)
- Biotinylated T-cell ligand cocktail components

### Equipment

- 0.22 μm Corning filter system
- 50 mL Steriflip filters
- Biosafety Cabinet (BSC)
- Analytical balance
- 1.5-mL LoBind microcentrifuge tubes
- Bath sonicator
- 1-mL pipettes
- -80 °C freezer
- -20 °C freezer
- Brightfield microscope
- Incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2)
- Flow cytometer (for FACS)
- MACS separation system (e.g., LS columns)
- Gastight glass syringes
- Round-bottom glass culture tubes
- Nitrogen gas stream with in-line 0.2 μm filter
- Vacuum chamber/desiccator
- Vortex mixer
- Liposome extruder apparatus with 0.1 μm polycarbonate membrane
- Glass extruder syringes
- 250 mL Erlenmeyer flasks
- 50 mm magnetic stir bars
- Magnetic hotplate stirrer
- Glass thermometer
- Parafilm
- Reflux condenser or Saran wrap
- 1 L Erlenmeyer flask
- Sterile polypropylene sample containers
- Oven (100 °C)

### Safety & Sterility

- β-Mercaptoethanol is volatile and hazardous; use in a fume hood with proper PPE.
- All steps involving biological material exposure to the environment must be performed in a Biosafety Cabinet (BSC) to maintain sterility, except for end-point analytics on samples that may be discarded immediately after.
- Steps involving chloroform, HCl, and dried MSR powder must be performed in a fume hood with appropriate PPE. HCl is corrosive; handle with care and use high-temperature protective equipment when handling hot solutions.
- Dried MSRs are easily aerosolized; handle in a fume hood with proper PPE.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-culture preparation

1. To 435 mL of RPMI-1640, add 50 mL heat-inactivated FBS (final concentration 10% vol/vol), 5 mL penicillin/streptomycin (final concentration 1% vol/vol), 5 mL 100X sodium pyruvate, 5 mL 100X non-essential amino acids, 1,124 mg cell culture grade HEPES (final concentration 20 mM), and 1.9 µL β-mercaptoethanol (final concentration 50 µM). Filter the solution through a 0.22 μm Corning filter system and store at 4 °C for up to 2 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: β-Mercaptoethanol is volatile and hazardous. Use in a fume hood with proper PPE. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
2. To 45 mL of heat-inactivated FBS, add 5 mL of DMSO (final concentration 10% vol/vol). Sterilize by filtration through a 0.22 µm filter and store at 4 °C for up to 2 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
3. To 500 mL of 1X PBS, add 2.5 g BSA (final concentration 0.5% wt/vol). Ensure the BSA is fully dissolved. Remove 2 mL of the solution, then add 2 mL of EDTA (0.5M stock, final concentration 2 mM) to the remaining solution. Filter the solution through a 0.22 μm filter and store at 4 °C for up to 2 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
4. To 50 mL 1X PBS, add 125 mg BSA (final concentration 0.25% wt/vol). Filter through a 0.22 μm filter (e.g., 50 mL Steriflip) and store at 4 °C for up to 2 months. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
5. Centrifuge a vial of BioLegend recombinant human IL-2 (typically available at 0.2 mg/mL) and store in single 10 µL aliquots at -80 °C for up to 1 year. To prepare T-cell media containing 30 U/mL IL-2, add the appropriate amount of IL-2 based on the specific activity of each lot. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
6. Reconstitute Streptavidin dry powder (obtained from VWR) in 1X PBS at 0.5 mg/mL. Confirm the final protein concentration using an appropriate method (e.g., protein absorbance at 280 nm). Aliquot and store at −20 °C for up to 6 months. Avoid multiple freeze-thaw cycles. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->

## Activation of primary human T cells with APC-ms

### 0.5 h

1. In the BSC, add prewarmed T-cell media to 24-well tissue culture plates (or another appropriate culture vessel) at the volume defined in Table 7 or Table 8 under the column designated as 'T-cell-media backfill'. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare a cell suspension of PBMCs or purified Pan T cells at the appropriate concentration in prewarmed T-cell media, as listed in Table 7 or Table 8. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. Mix the cell suspension to obtain a homogeneous suspension and add 100 µL to each well as listed in Table 7 or Table 8. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
4. Mix the APC-ms suspension gently but thoroughly with a hand pipette. Add the appropriate volume of the resuspended APC-ms solution to each well as defined in Table 7 or Table 8. Upon adding APC-ms to the cell culture, gently mix the culture suspension containing the cells and APC-ms. Transfer the seeded culture vessel to an incubator set at 37 °C and 5% CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Ensure the culture suspension containing APC-ms and T cells is mixed to ensure even distribution. After seeding, T cells interact with APC-ms and become activated. It is critical that these interactions are not disrupted for the first 24 hours post-seeding. During this time, do not mix cultures and handle the vessels gently if they need to be moved. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->
5. Seeded cells may be phenotypically characterized via FACS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S06 -->
6. Post-seeding, cultures may be imaged via brightfield microscopy after cells and APC-ms rods have settled to the bottom of the culture vessel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S07 -->

## Expansion and enrichment of T cells following activation

### ~2 weeks

1. Expand T cells following polyclonal activation with APC-ms according to the guidelines in Table 9. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S01 -->
2. Restimulate T cells with fresh APC-ms as desired. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Do not recommend restimulating the cultures until at least 7 days of culture have passed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Starting on approximately day 6, it is recommended that T cells are maintained at a cell density between 0.2 × 10^6 and 1 × 10^6 cells/mL for tissue plate cultures. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S05 -->
3. When the concentration of T cells exceeds this level, transfer the cell suspension containing T cells and degrading APC-ms to a larger vessel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S06 -->
4. Starting on or before day 7, perform media additions with T-cell media supplemented with 30 U/mL IL-2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S07 -->
5. Analytical and functional assays can be performed at desired timepoints (Box 2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S08 -->

### ~2+ weeks

1. Culture cells following antigen-specific activation with APC-ms according to the guidelines in Table 10. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S01 -->
2. Perform restimulations as desired. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Do not recommend restimulating the cultures until after at least 7 days of culture. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Starting on approximately day 6, it is recommended that T cells are maintained at a cell density between 0.2 × 10^6 and 1 × 10^6 cells/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S04 -->
3. If the cell concentration exceeds this level, the cell suspension containing T cells and degrading APC-ms should be transferred to a larger vessel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S05 -->
4. Starting on or before day 7, perform media additions with T-cell media supplemented with 30 U/mL of IL-2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S06 -->
5. Analytical and functional assays can be performed at desired timepoints (Box 2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S07 -->

## Fabrication of APC-ms

### 4 h

1. Weigh out the appropriate amount of MSRs (from Step 24) in a 1.5-mL LoBind microcentrifuge tube (or another appropriately sized tube) using an analytical balance. We recommend using at least 10 mg MSRs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Resuspend the MSRs in Milli-Q water at 50 mg/mL (e.g., 200 µL water per 10 mg MSRs). Submerge the MSR suspension in a bath sonicator for 1-3 seconds. Gently mix the MSR suspension using a 1-mL pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: If necessary, repeat the sonication (mixing) step until the MSRs are fully resuspended and the suspension can be pipetted through a standard 1-mL pipette tip without clogging. Dilute MSRs in Milli-Q water and visualize under brightfield microscopy. MSRs should appear morphologically similar and nonfragmented. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
3. Retrieve an appropriately sized aliquot of 0.2 mg/mL IL-2 from the −80 °C freezer and thaw it on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->
4. Add 30 µL of Milli-Q water to a 1.5 mL LoBind microcentrifuge tube (referred to hereafter as the assembly tube). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S05 -->
5. Transfer 10 µL of 0.2 mg/mL IL-2 stock (2 µg) to the assembly tube and mix using a pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S06 -->
6. Transfer 10 µL of the 50 mg/mL MSR suspension to the assembly tube (500 µg MSRs) and gently mix using a pipette. Allow IL-2 to adsorb for just over an hour at room temperature with gentle mixing every 10 minutes (7 mixes in total). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S07 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: After adding the MSR suspension, perform all mixing steps using a hand pipette. Avoid vortexing or other vigorous mixing methods so that the high-aspect-ratio microrods do not fracture. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S08 -->
7. Add 100 µL of liposomes (from Step 33; 250 µg lipid) to the assembly tube and gently mix. Allow the lipids to coat the MSRs for an hour at room temperature with gentle mixing every 10 minutes (7 mixes in total). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S09 -->
8. Add 850 µL of 1× PBS to the assembly tube and mix gently. Centrifuge the material suspension at 700g for 5 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S10 -->
9. Using a hand pipette, carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the pellet. Wash the pellet with 1,000 µL of 1× PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S11 -->
10. Wash the material twice by repeating Steps 49-50 (twice). After the final wash, carefully aspirate the supernatant using a hand pipette without disturbing the pellet. Resuspend the pellet in 200 µL of APC-ms-blocking buffer. Block for 10 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S12 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: The blocking buffer volume in Step 51 determines the streptavidin concentration during cue conjugation (in Step 54), which is a critical parameter for attaching T-cell ligands without extensive material aggregation. Carefully scale this volume based on the batch size. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S13 -->
11. Retrieve an appropriately sized aliquot of streptavidin from the −20 °C freezer and thaw it on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S14 -->
12. Prepare biotinylated T-cell ligand cocktail in a 1.5-mL LoBind microcentrifuge tube for the desired formulation as defined in Table 5. Prepare and dilute the biotinylated T-cell ligand stock as needed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S15 -->
13. Gently mix the material suspension, then add an appropriate amount of streptavidin to the assembly tube and mix (Table 5). Allow streptavidin to bind to biotinylated lipids for 10 minutes at room temperature with gentle mixing every 2 minutes (5 mixes in total). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S16 -->
14. After 10 minutes, add the appropriate amount of the T-cell ligand cocktail to the assembly tube and mix. Allow surface ligands to bind to streptavidin for 40 minutes at room temperature with gentle mixing every 10 minutes (5 mixes in total). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S17 -->
15. Add 800 µL APC-ms-blocking buffer to the assembly tube and mix. Centrifuge the material suspension at 700g for 5 minutes at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S18 -->
16. Carefully aspirate the supernatant using a hand pipette without disturbing the pellet. Resuspend the pellet in 1,000 µL of 1× PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S19 -->
17. Wash the material twice by repeating Steps 57-58 (twice). After the final wash, carefully aspirate the supernatant using a hand pipette without disturbing the pellet. Resuspend the pellet in 300 µL of T-cell media. Visualize APC-ms under brightfield microscopy. The individual rods should appear morphologically similar and nonfragmented. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S20 -->
> **Operational constraint:** PAUSE POINT: Fully-assembled IL-2-loaded APC-ms have been used immediately following fabrication to activate T cells. For a more detailed discussion of the APC-ms shelf life, see the ‘Experimental design'. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S21 -->

## Isolation of PBMCs and T cells

### 2.5 h

1. Prepare a BSC by wiping down all working surfaces with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol. Wipe down all materials with 70% ethanol prior to transferring them into the BSC. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: All steps in which biological material is exposed to the environment must be performed in the BSC to maintain sterility, with the exception of manipulations for end-point analytics on samples (Box 2) that may be appropriately discarded immediately after. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
2. Isolate PBMCs from deidentified leukapheresis donors (see ‘Reagent setup'). Wash the cell suspensions at least twice with excess PBS and count the cells. Cell viability is expected to be >90%. The number of PBMCs required will depend on the scale of the experiment and a number of material conditions. Freeze unused PBMCs at between 1 × 10^7 to 1 × 10^8 cells/vial using the freezing media (see ‘Reagent setup') and store in liquid nitrogen. Cryopreserved cells should be used within 1 year. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** cCRITICAL STEP Carefully note the density of platelets. If the platelet density is high (e.g., >~10 platelets per PBMC71), repeat the PBS washes. The presence of platelets may inﬂuence downstream T-cell expansion. It is also recommended that PBMCs are phenotypically evaluated via ﬂow cytometry to determine starting cell populations. In the case of antigen-speciﬁc T-cell enrichment, the frequency of reactive T-cell clones should be measured via MHC tetramer or multimer staining (Box 2 and Table 4). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->

### 0.5 h

> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL: PBMCs can be either purified to T cells or activated using APC-ms. For the T-cell-selection method, follow Steps 36-40. For the activation method, proceed directly to Step 60. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S01 -->
1. In the BSC, thaw ~1 × 10^8 PBMCs or use fresh PBMCs (from Step 35). Perform a cell count: viability is expected to be >90%. Keep the PBMCs cooled on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S02 -->
2. Precool MACS buffer on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S03 -->
3. Based on the cell count obtained in Step 36, select for Pan T cells using the manufacturer-defined protocol and with any manufacturer-recommended equipment (e.g., LS columns). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: We recommend the isolation of Pan T cells from at least 5 × 10^7 PBMCs. We routinely collect 2 × 10^7 to 6 × 10^7 Pan T cells from 1 × 10^8 PBMCs (20-60%) depending on the donor. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S05 -->
4. Prewarm T-cell media in a 37 °C water bath. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S06 -->
5. Centrifuge the T-cell suspension at 300g for 5 minutes at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S07 -->
6. Carefully aspirate the supernatant. Resuspend the cell pellet in T-cell media and perform a cell count. T-cell viability is expected to be >95%. It is recommended that the purity of the preparation be confirmed via flow cytometry. Purified T cells can either be cryopreserved or activated using APC-ms. If not preserved, the cell suspension should be cultured with APC-ms or control APCs as soon as possible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S08 -->
7. PAUSE POINT: To cryopreserve the cells, freeze them at ~1 × 10^8 cells/vial using the freezing media (see ‘Reagent setup'), and store in liquid nitrogen. Cryopreserved cells can be stored for up to 1 year. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S09 -->

## Preparation of liposomes for MSR coating

### 1 d

1. Using an appropriately sized gastight glass syringe, transfer the appropriate volume of each chloroform-dissolved lipid into a round-bottom glass culture tube to achieve the desired lipid composition (Table 4). Prepare the desired stock of Biotinyl Cap PE via dilution into chloroform. This protocol assumes a 2.5 mg lipid batch size. Lipid input (as defined in Table 4) can be scaled linearly to prepare larger liposome batch sizes. Rinse syringe with isopropyl alcohol, or switch to a new syringe for each new lipid component. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: Steps 25-27 should be performed in a fume hood with appropriate PPE. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** It is critical to measure the volume of each lipid component precisely. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S03 -->
2. Evaporate the bulk chloroform solvent under a gentle stream of nitrogen gas via a syringe-capped hose equipped with an in-line 0.2 μm filter, leaving a translucent film on the bottom of the culture tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S04 -->
3. Transfer the lipid film-containing glass culture tube to a vacuum chamber. Vacuum overnight to evaporate the residual chloroform. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S05 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Lipid films may be stored in a vacuum desiccator for up to 6 months and can be used as needed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S06 -->
4. Remove the glass culture tube from the vacuum chamber and resuspend the lipid film in 1× PBS at 2.5 mg lipid per 1 mL PBS. If sterile liposome suspensions are desired, Steps 28-32 should be performed in a BSC with sterile and/or autoclaved materials. Check for endotoxin in the final liposome suspension as needed (e.g., using the LAL reagent test kit). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S07 -->
5. Cover the tube with Parafilm and mix the lipid suspension vigorously for 30 seconds (or until no visible lipid film remains on the bottom of the tube) using a vortex mixer set at maximum speed. Repeat every 10 minutes for an hour (7 mixes in total). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S08 -->
6. Assemble the extrusion apparatus as described by the manufacturer using a 0.1 μm polycarbonate membrane. Pre-wet the glass extruder syringes by aspirating and dispensing sterile 1× PBS. Pre-wet the extruder by passing 1 mL of sterile 1× PBS through the apparatus. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S09 -->
7. Aspirate the lipid suspension into a pre-wet extruder syringe and extrude the suspension. Pass the lipid suspension through the extruder from one syringe to the other a total of 21 times. The lipid suspension should become increasingly transparent. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S10 -->
8. Carefully remove the syringe containing the extruded liposome suspension from the extruder and transfer the suspension to an appropriately sized vessel (e.g., a 1.5-mL LoBind microcentrifuge tube). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S11 -->
> **Operational constraint:** The liposome suspension may be stored for up to 2 weeks at 4 °C. Note that over time, the liposome stability will vary depending on the lipid composition. Prior to use, vortex the liposome suspension and validate the size and dispersity to ensure products remain within working range. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S13 -->

## Procedure

### After 10 min

1. Add 800 µL APC-ms-blocking buffer to the assembly tube and mix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S112 -->
2. Centrifuge the material suspension at 700g for 5 min at room temperature. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S113 -->
3. Wash the material twice by repeating Steps 57-58 (twice). After the final wash, carefully aspirate the supernatant using a hand pipette without disturbing the pellet. Resuspend the pellet in 300 µL of T-cell media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:S114 -->

## Synthesis of high-aspect-ratio MSRs

### 4 d

1. Add 130 mL of Milli-Q water to a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask (referred to hereafter as the reaction flask). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Using a sterile disposable spatula, weigh 4 g of the P123 and add it to the reaction flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Weigh the P123 precisely. The amount of the templating surfactant used in the reaction will impact the physical attributes of the material. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
3. Add a 50 mm magnetic stir bar to the reaction flask. Place the reaction flask on the magnetic hotplate stirrer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: Steps 4-22 should be performed in a fume hood with appropriate PPE. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
4. Using a glass pipette, carefully add 20 mL of concentrated HCl to the reaction flask by submerging the tip of the pipette into the reaction volume and slowly dispensing. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: HCl is corrosive and should be handled in a fume hood with proper PPE and care. Use appropriate high-temperature protective equipment when handling. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
5. Set the spin speed to 600 r.p.m. and the temperature to 40 °C. Using an appropriate clamping apparatus, place a glass thermometer into the reaction flask. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Ensure that the stir bar is centered and stably spinning in place. Ensure that the glass thermometer is submerged to approximately half the depth of the reaction volume. The thermometer should be deep enough to accurately measure the temperature of the solution but it should not interfere with the stir bar. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
6. Cover the reaction flask with Parafilm. Allow the P123 to fully dissolve and the temperature to equilibrate at 40 °C. This should take approximately 1-2 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
7. Remove the Parafilm cover and add 9.2 mL of tetraethyl orthosilicate directly to the reaction solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
8. Cover the reaction flask with Parafilm and allow the reaction to proceed at 40 °C for 20 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: This process determines the macrostructure of the material. Within 15 minutes, the solution-to-gel transition should be visible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
9. After 20 hours, remove the Parafilm and attach a reflux condenser to the reaction flask to prevent excessive evaporation of the reaction solution. Alternatively, the reaction flask can be covered using Saran wrap. Raise the temperature of the reaction to 100 °C while monitoring with the glass thermometer until it equilibrates at 100 °C. Maintain stirring at 600 r.p.m. Allow the hydrothermal treatment to process for 20 hours. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: This process determines the mesopore structure of the material. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S15 -->
10. After 20 hours, remove the reaction flask from the magnetic hotplate stirrer and allow to cool at ambient temperature for 30 minutes or until warm to the touch (<40 °C). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S16 -->
11. Swirl the reaction flask gently until the settled MSRs are visibly in suspension. Carefully pour the MSR suspension into the 0.22 μm Corning filter system or an equivalent filtration apparatus. Filter the MSR suspension under vacuum until all the liquid has been filtered. The solid material that remains in filter is the MSR product. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S17 -->
> **Operational constraint:** PAUSE POINT: The dried MSRs contain P123 surfactant but may be stored for up to 1 year at room temperature (20-25 °C) under low humidity, or in a vacuum desiccator, before surfactant extraction. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S18 -->
12. Add 500 mL 200-proof ethanol and 5 mL concentrated HCl to a 1 L Erlenmeyer flask (referred to hereafter as the extraction flask). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S19 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: HCl is corrosive and should be handled in a fume hood with proper PPE and care. Use appropriate high-temperature protective equipment when handling. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S20 -->
13. Add a 50 mm magnetic stir bar to the extraction flask. Place the extraction flask on the magnetic hotplate stirrer. Set the spin speed to 600 r.p.m. and the temperature to 70 °C. Using an appropriate clamping apparatus, place a glass thermometer into the reaction flask to monitor the reaction temperature until it equilibrates at 70 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S21 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Ensure that the stir bar is centered and stably spinning in place. Ensure that the glass thermometer is submerged to approximately half the depth of the reaction volume. The thermometer should be deep enough to accurately measure the temperature of the solution but it should not interfere with the stir bar. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S22 -->
14. Gently dislodge the dried MSRs (Step 13) from the filter by lightly tapping the side of the filter and transfer them into the extraction flask using a clean spatula as needed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S23 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CAUTION: Dried MSRs are easily aerosolized and should be handled in a fume hood with proper PPE and care. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S24 -->
15. Cover the extraction flask with Parafilm and stir the mixture at 600 r.p.m. for 24 hours at 70 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S25 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: This process removes the surfactant template from the MSRs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S26 -->
16. After 24 hours, carefully pour the MSR suspension into a 0.22 μm Corning filter system, or an equivalent filtration system. Filter the MSR suspension under vacuum until all the liquid has been filtered. The solid material that remains in filter is the MSR product. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S27 -->
17. Wash the filtered solids by adding 200 mL 200-proof ethanol to the filter and allowing the liquid to filter through under vacuum. Repeat so that the MSR product is washed with a total of 600 mL ethanol (3 washes). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S28 -->
18. Place lid on filter and allow the MSR product to dry at room temperature for 1 hour. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S29 -->
19. Carefully transfer the MSR product to a sterile polypropylene sample container. With the lid loosely screwed on, place the sample container in an oven set at 100 °C for at least 24 hours to thoroughly dry the MSR product. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S30 -->
> **Operational constraint:** CRITICAL STEP: Residual moisture in MSR product can mediate hydrolytic degradation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S31 -->
20. Secure the lid and store the dry MSR product. Performing Steps 1-24 should generate 4.6 ± 0.1 g of MSR (avg ± s.d.), which should be enough material to theoretically activate >110 T cells. The dry powder should be characterized to ensure consistency between synthesized MSR batches. Box 1 highlights material characterizations that are routinely performed. Table 2 highlights expected physical properties from a batch of synthesized MSRs. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S32 -->
> **Operational constraint:** The dry MSR product can be stored at room temperature under low humidity, or in a vacuum desiccator, for up to 1 year. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S33 -->
